newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says 1995 energy consumption lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says 1995 energy consumption lower.

text.p: Mexico consumed less energy in 1995 than the previous year, the Energy Ministry said Tuesday in a report. National energy consumption fell 2.1 percent from 1994, and in per capita terms fell 3.2 percent, it said.
Energy use in 1995 was divided between 38.9 percent for transportation, 36.2 percent for the industrial sector, 20.6 percent for residential and commercial use and 2.6 percent for agriculture uses.
"It is necessary to reinforce the savings programs and efficient use of energy," the ministry said.
Energy exports rose 0.4 percent in 1995 from the previous year, while imports fell 20.9 percent because of a reduced demand for refined petroleum by-products, mainly fuel oil, the ministry said.

"In 1995 the performance of the sector responded to several factors, among them the behavior of the Mexican economy and the evolution of the international economy, especially the petroleum market," the report said.
Natural gas consumption from 1980 to 1995 grew three percent annually, compared to overall energy consumption growth of 0.7 percent, the document said.
